classification.difficultyReason: Reframe each nominal metre as 96 actual centimetres, apply this scale factor to the entire mixed-number purchase and convert the resulting length to metres.

content.prompt: Ava thought she had bought $3\frac{1}{2}$ m of cloth from the market. When she got home, she found that the stall holder had used a ruler that was 4 cm short of 1 m. What was the real length, in metres, of Ava’s cloth?

answer.worked:
Each supposed metre measures $100-4=96$ cm, or $\frac{96}{100}$ m.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Actual length}&=3\frac12\times\frac{96}{100}\text{ m}\\\text{Actual length}&=\frac72\times\frac{24}{25}\text{ m}\\\text{Actual length}&=\frac{84}{25}\text{ m}\\\text{Actual length}&=3.36\text{ m}\end{align*}$$
